newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp-minimum reserves essential for ECB.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp-minimum reserves essential for ECB.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Monday that it was essential that the future European Central Bank (ECB) use a minimum reserve system.
In a speech to bankers in Kiel, Krupp also said that the Bundesbank was keen for the ECB to use three-month tender at a fixed interest rate to provide extra liquidity to the market.
"We have not succeeded in this so far, as according to the plans of the European Monetary Institute this transaction should not set any signals on interest rate policy," he said.

Krupp said that whereas the Bundesbank was in favour in principle of the longer-term three-month tender, it would have preferred the bank to offer funds only against a deposit of privately issued paper.
The German central bank was also somewhat concerned about a suggestion that shares could be used as collateral, he said.

The European Monetary Institute, the forerunner to the European Central Bank, mapped out its draft for the policy tools of the future ECB last month. But final decisions on the details will only be taken once the ECB is set up in 1998.

Krupp said he believed it would be sensible for the ECB to use a combination of monetary policy targeting and inflation targeting. The decision on the ECB's precise policy stance will also be made in 1998.
